1|R8.headline: ALVIA 2384 likely hit by derailed Iryo; no emergency dispatch for it yet

hypotheses.statement: ALVIA 2384 collided with the fouling Iryo coaches on track 2 and needs rescue.
A rail discontinuity on track 1 near PK 318.68 caused the IRYO 6189 derailment. Each warning sign was below its own alarm threshold.
The Iryo driver's 'catenary snag' was the derailment; the catenary voltage loss is a consequence of it.

1|R9.headline: ALVIA 2384 almost certainly hit: first 112 call from its passengers, no emergency dispatch yet

hypotheses.statement: ALVIA 2384 struck the derailed Iryo coaches fouling track 2 and is itself badly damaged, with crew incapacitated.
The derailment started at a rail discontinuity on track 1 near PK 318.68 that earlier signals pointed to, each below its own threshold.
Emergency response is currently sized and located for one train only, so the Alvia site may go unattended.

0|R15.summary: Major two-train derailment at Adamuz, PK ~318.2–318.9, both tracks. Sim time 20:35. IRYO 6189 (track 1, 294 on board) derailed and is fouling the adjacent track, with fire, injuries and at least one passenger death reported by its driver [R7][R11]. ALVIA 2384 (track 2, 184 on board) has also derailed, with 'half the train overturned' per its train manager [R13], confirmed by Adif Sevilla [R14]. The first medical unit reached the Iryo at 20:02 [R10] and the first medical team reached the Alvia at 20:35, about 52 minutes after the collision [R15]. The incident began at 19:43:37, when S613 (track 2) dropped to STOP on loss of point detection as ALVIA 2384 approached [I4], followed by a catenary voltage drop in the Adamuz section [R0]. The ALVIA driver did not answer two calls [R5][R6]. At 19:49 the CTC told the Iryo driver 'no train is coming' [R7], and at 20:09 Adif CPS wrongly told 112 Madrid that the Alvia had not derailed [R12]. That statement was later contradicted [R13][R14], but there is no record that 112 was corrected. AVLO 2181 is stopped at PK 309.0 on track 2 with no catenary voltage [R4]; its passenger count is unknown. All 14 recommendations (REC-001 to REC-014) still show as pending with no recorded decision.
unresolved: No recorded traffic stop on either track. The Iryo driver urgently requested one [R7]; REC-001 and REC-002 are still pending. Confirm both tracks are blocked, roughly PK 300–340.
112 Madrid was told the Alvia did not derail [R12], and no correction is recorded. REC-014 (correct 112 Madrid and 112 Andalucía: Alvia derailed, half overturned, 184 on board) is still pending.
There is no confirmation that the catenary is de-energised and earthed, yet responders are now on site at both trains [R10][R15]. REC-007 is still pending.

Casualties: one death [R11], plus fire and injuries on the Iryo [R7]. The Alvia's condition is unknown beyond 'half overturned' [R13]. No casualty counts are recorded for either train (478 people on board in total).
ALVIA 2384 driver: the record shows two unanswered calls [R5][R6] and no later contact with or information about the driver.

Emergency mobilisation was recorded for the Iryo only [R8]. There is no record of explicit dispatch to the Alvia (REC-010) or of 112 Andalucía being notified (REC-006); responders reached the Alvia only at 20:35 [R15].
AVLO 2181 is stopped at PK 309.0, track 2, without power [R4]. Its passenger count and onward handling are not recorded.
The cause is undetermined: loss of point detection at S613 [I4] and the power loss [R0] occurred within seconds of each other.

1|R15.summary: Sim time 20:35, 18 Jan 2026. Major incident at Adamuz, PK ~318.7, affecting both tracks [I2][I4][R0]. IRYO 6189 (294 on board, track 1, now PK 318.2) derailed at 19:43:34: coach 6 first axle, then coaches 7–8. It is fouling the adjacent track 2, with fire reported and at least one passenger death [I2][R7][R11]. ALVIA 2384 (184 on board, track 2, now PK 318.85) is also derailed, with 'half the train overturned'. This was confirmed by its train manager [R13] and by Adif Sevilla [R14]. Its telemetry was lost while braking [I6], and the driver did not answer two calls [R5][R6]; the driver's condition remains unknown. Emergency response: Adif mobilised emergency services at 19:50 [R8]. The first medical unit reached the Iryo at 20:02 [R10]. The first medical team reached the Alvia only at 20:35, about 52 minutes after the collision [R15]. At 20:09:58 Adif CPS told 112 Madrid that the Alvia had NOT derailed [R12]; this was false, and the record holds no correction to 112. Catenary power was lost in the Adamuz section [R0]. AVLO 2181 is stopped on track 2 at PK 309.0 with no catenary voltage [R4]; its number on board is unknown. Likely cause (hypothesis, high confidence): a rail discontinuity on track 1, PK 318.4–319.0. Precursors were all below their own alarm thresholds: a union warning [P1], an inspection reading [P2], a track-circuit voltage drop [P3], a driver vibration report [P4], and wheel impacts on 3 trains at PK 318.68 [P5][P6][P7]. A rail break is suspected but not confirmed.
unresolved: No record that traffic is formally stopped and protected on both tracks PK 300–340. REC-007, REC-009 and REC-011 are still pending. AVLO 2181 [R4] and any following trains must be held. Track 2 is fouled [R7] and both trains are on site.
112 Madrid was told the Alvia did not derail [R12]. No correction to 112 Madrid or 112 Andalucía is logged (REC-021 and REC-015 pending). This risks under-resourcing the 184 people on the Alvia.

ALVIA 2384 driver unreachable after 2 calls [R5][R6]; condition unknown. Casualty status on both trains is incomplete: one death on the Iryo is reported [R11], fire was reported on the Iryo [R7], and the Alvia is half overturned [R13].
Medical response to the Alvia arrived only at 20:35 [R15]. Whether resources are sufficient for both sites (up to 478 people) is unconfirmed (REC-014 and REC-018 pending).
Catenary in the Adamuz section is de-energised [R0]. No record of isolation or earthing for responders working near the overhead line.
